mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals robust economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO MoM < -2% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, which typically leads to reduced economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy in strong labor market
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS MoM > 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% MoM signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS MoM < -1% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and industrial production (INDPRO) is flat or declining, it signals a contraction in both housing and manufacturing sectors, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY < -10% and INDPRO flat or declining
failure_condition: If HOUST YoY < -10% and INDPRO is flat or declining, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.
